name: Sue Gross
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Sue Gross is the ex-wife of PIMCO cofounder and billionaire Bill Gross. The two divorced in 2017 after 32 years of marriage.
Gross walked away with roughly $1.3 billion, including a $36 million house in Laguna Beach and half of the couple's art collection.
After the divorce, she sold a Picasso painting for $35 million and purchased a number of properties in Orange County.
In 2017, Sue Gross started her own charitable vehicle, Sue J. Gross Foundation.
Previously the couple had run the William and Sue Gross Family Foundation, which supported Doctors Without Borders, Columbia U. and Duke U.
forbes_facts: Gross apparently got custody of two of she and her ex-husband's three cats in their divorce settlement.

name: Christoph Henkel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Christoph Henkel is the founding partner of investment firm Canyon Equity.
With brands like Persil, Schwarzkopf and Fa, and over $20 billion in annual revenue, Henkel is among the world's biggest cleaning product companies.
After the death of his father Konrad in 1999, Christoph Henkel inherited his interest in Henkel AG and became the largest single stockholder in the company.
He also invests in tech, biotech and movie-production companies, and has real estate holdings in Europe and the U.S.
Canyon Equity has acquired or developed luxury resorts in Fiji, Utah, Wyoming and New Mexico, with more planned in Costa Rica, Mexico and Malibu, CA.
forbes_facts: Henkel co-founded Los Angeles-based production company Cineville; actors in its films have included Kevin Spacey, Sean Penn and Selma Hayek.
An outdoorsman and active in acquiring land for conservation, he is married to the German art dealer and collector Katrin Bellinger.

name: Chirayu Amin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Pharma tycoon Chirayu Amin's Alembic Pharmaceuticals is one of India's oldest pharma companies.
Alembic was founded by Amin's grandfather in 1907 to make tincture and alcohol.
Today, Alembic gets more than a third of its annual revenue from the domestic market selling generic drugs, including popular cough syrup Glycodin.
While Amin is chairman and chief executive, his three sons work in different parts of the business.
forbes_facts: Amin is the brother-in-law of consumer goods billionaire Harsh Mariwala.
Amin was head of the Indian Premier League for 17 months after its founder Lalit Modi was sacked in 2010.

name: Shao Qinxiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2012-2026)
forbes_bio: Shao Qinxiang chairs Zhejiang Garden Bio-chemical High-tech, a supplier of pharmaceuticals and animal nutrition products.
Shao is the controlling shareholder of parent Garden Group, which was founded in 2000.
Garden Group was founded as a candle factory and then a garment manufacturer. It has since diversified into pharmaceuticals, energy and other fields.

name: Osman Kibar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2017-2023); Wikidata (2020); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Osman Kibar is the founder and CEO of San Diego-based biotech firm Samumed.
Samumed raised $438 million in August 2018 to further its work developing drugs to reverse aging, claiming a valuation of $12.4 billion.
The names of investors in the round were not disclosed.
While getting a Ph.D. from the University of California, San Diego, he founded two companies, but did not have a management role at either.
He then founded Samumed in 2008 in a Pfizer incubator, but had a falling out with the drug giant; Samumed now operates independent of Pfizer.
forbes_facts: Kibar was born in Izmir, Turkey, on the Aegean Coast and met most of his fellow Samumed executives at boarding school in Istanbul.
In 2006 Kibar won the first poker tournament he ever played in, and a year later came in second out of 3,000 players at a World Series of Poker tournament.

name: Anna Maria Braun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Anna Maria Braun is CEO of medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
A sixth-generation family member, she owns 10% of the company and also serves as president of its Asian/Pacific operations.
Her father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
forbes_facts: Anna Maria is a member of the board of Dr. August Oetker KG, a $9 billion (sales) conglomerate with interests in food, beverages, financial services and hotels.
Her billionaire brother Otto Philipp Braun was responsible for the company's Iberian Peninsula and Latin American regions before stepping down in February 2017.

name: Chen Bangdong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2007-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Bangdong is vice chairman of Sieyuan Electric, a provider of electrical solutions and services.
Chen has worked at the company since 1993.
The company went public in 2004.
The company has 9,456 employees.

name: Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani is the chairman of Al Faisal Holding, one of Qatar's biggest conglomerates, which he founded in 1964.
It owns more than 20 hotels around the world, including the St. Regis in Washington, D.C. and Miami, and the W Hotel in London.
Al Faisal Holding also has a majority stake in publicly-traded Aamal, which owns real estate in Qatar and sells medical supplies and pharmaceuticals.
Al Thani started selling car parts in Doha at age 16. He became the sole distributor of Bridgestone tires in the 1960s.
forbes_facts: Al Thani is a distant relative of the Qatari royal family.
A museum in Doha houses his collection of more than 15,000 artifacts, including antique cars, ancient coins and Islamic art.

name: Zhong Ruonong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025)
forbes_bio: Zhong Ruonong chairs Shenzhen-ilsted Zhuzhou Hongda Electronics.
Zhuzhou Hongda Electronics makes electronic components including  capacitors, inductors and resistors.
Husband Zeng Jijiang is general manager of the listed company.

name: Brian Roberts
sec_insider_companies: COMCAST CORP (CMCSA) - Chairman of Board & CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Brian Roberts is chairman and CEO of media and technology company Comcast.
His father Ralph Roberts (d. 2015) was the founder of Comcast, where Brian Roberts did his first internship at age 15.
Brian Roberts became president in 1990 at age 31; seven years later, his father transferred the bulk of his Comcast voting shares to him.
He now controls nearly a third of the company's voting power thanks to his super voting shares.
Comcast acquired the NHL's Philadelphia Flyers in 2016 and UK-based media and telecom conglomerate Sky in 2018.
forbes_facts: A top ranked squash player, Roberts earned a gold medal with the U.S. team at the Maccabiah Games in Israel in 2005 and silver medals in 1981, 1985 and 1997.

name: Daniel Calugar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Dan Calugar is a private investor based in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Calugar worked as a tax lawyer in Atlanta the late 1970s and 1980s before switching to investing in mutual funds.
He has invested using data-driven strategies across mutual funds, stocks, hedge funds, structured fixed income, volatility and managed futures.
He now primarily invests in an externally managed energy strategy and an in-house algorithmic stock trading program he developed internally.
In 2003, he settled alleged charges of fraud through improper late trading and market timing with the SEC for $225 million. He did not admit or deny the charges.
forbes_facts: Calugar attended the Air Force Academy and is a commercial pilot with more than 3,500 hours.
Calugar has flown over 200 Angel Flight missions, providing free air transport for passengers in need of medical treatment and for community service.

name: Ilson Mateus
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: A former gold miner, Ilson Mateus built up supermarket chain Grupo Mateus and took it public in October 2020.
The company is controlled by Mateus and his ex-wife, Maria Barros Pinheiro, who is a former billionaire.
Now Brazil's fourth-biggest food retailer, Grupo Mateus operates more than 200 stores throughout the country's northern and northeastern regions.
Grupo Mateus operates in 90 cities across Brazil and had revenues of $4.4 billion in 2023.
His fortune includes his two sons' stakes in Grupo Mateus.

name: Li Xiaohua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2024); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (1999-2026)
forbes_bio: Li Xiaohua is the vice chairman of Shenzhen-listed Yunnan Energy New Material, a supplier of paper packaging materials and polypropylene film.
Clients include Panasonic, LG Chemical and Comtemporary Amperex Technology.
Li graduated from the University of Massachusetts with a major in polymer materials in 1993.
He worked for World-Pak Corp. in the U.S. after graduation until 1996.
His brother Paul Xiaoming Lee, a U.S. citizen, is the chairman of Yunnan Energy New Material and is also a billionaire.

name: Bret Johnsen

forbes_bio: Bret Johnsen is the chief financial officer of SpaceX.
Johnsen joined the rocket and satellite company in 2011, after serving as CFO of semiconductor firm Mindspeed Technologies.
He holds a 0.07% stake in SpaceX (including stock options).
